title: Logistics Coordinator
description:
Air Liquide began operations in Malaysia in 1927 and is one of the pioneers of the gas industry in Malaysia. Operating in 11 locations in Malaysia, comprising both sales offices and production facilities, Air Liquide supports our customers through providing innovative solutions at every step of their production, including industrial and specialty gases, energy solutions, application technologies and services. With a strong workforce of 400 employees and business growth through our recent acquisition with nationwide presence, this will provide an exciting experience and journey with the opportunity that is unique yet challenging to gauge the integration and synergy processes that will change the entire competition landscape in Malaysia.

Air Liquide Global Export Materials (ALGEM) is the Global Gas Sourcing and Supply Chain Platform of Air Liquide Group for electronic specialty materials and Industrial Merchant materials in APAC, managing more than 1,800 shipments a year, for all Air Liquide Affiliates in the world.

Based in Kuala Lumpur with antennas in all APAC operating affiliates, ALGEM manages International Supply Chains including supply planning, logistics design & execution for globally and regionally traded materials.

How will you CONTRIBUTE and GROW?

Reporting to the Inland SCM Manager, the Logistics Coordinator – Inland (Air Liquide Vietnam) is in charge of administering inland shipping transactions (from receiving ports/borders to facilities, and vice versa for returnable assets/cylinders) for Air Liquide Vietnam.

To that extent, the ALGEM Logistics Coordinator of Inland EAP (ALV) is responsible for:

(i) Inland Operations & Distribution: Organizing local transportation with internal/external logistics service providers and dispatching packages (both empty and full containers/cylinders/ISO tanks) in accordance with ALV’s operational needs, ensuring continuity of supply at optimized costs.

(ii) Shipment Tracking & Incident Management: Monitoring actual inland shipping progress and tracking ongoing movements. Promptly notifying key stakeholders and managing resolutions if any operational disruptions or delays occur.

(iii) Cross-Team & Regional Coordination: Coordinating seamlessly with local ALV operations/plant teams, customs brokers, and KL-based international logistics coordinators for smooth shipment handover at designated Vietnamese arrival ports/terminals to ALV facilities.

(iv) Documentation, Compliance & Invoicing: Preparing and managing all relevant inland transport documentation, handling local import/export and chemical permit applications (e.g., MOIT, local regulatory authorities), and issuing accurate invoices to dedicated affiliates in a timely manner.

(v) Stakeholder Communication: Ensuring timely, clear, and accurate communication with ALV and regional teams regarding shipment organization, delivery schedules, documentation, and potential operational hazards.

(vi) Continuous Improvement & Local Support: Supporting ad-hoc supply chain optimization projects, local business growth initiatives, and process standardization within Vietnam.

Candidate should be able to communicate effectively with cross-functional teams, including supply planners, asset managers, procurement, warehouse, commercial, and HSE teams within the ALGEM and ALV organizations, to achieve strategic goals in Safety, Quality, Reliability, and Efficiency.

The Logistics Coordinator – Inland is directly responsible for all inland logistics coordination within Vietnam, ensuring safe and compliant transport from port/border entry to ALV facilities and return loop management.

Are you a MATCH?

  • Extensive Experience in supply chain, order taking, logistics arrangement within the Chemical/Industrial Gas industry with a customer facing role. Knowledge of import/export of Vietnam and domestic delivery.

  • Experience in dealing with Dangerous Goods cargoes with freight forwarders and Vietnamese government.

  • Good communication in English and Vietnamese, very organized, rigorous, reliable, independent, transparent and diligent.

#LI-ML1

About Air Liquide

A world leader in gases, technologies and services for Industry and Health, Air Liquide is present in 78 countries with approximately 64,500 employees and serves more than 3.8 million customers and patients. Oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen are essential small molecules for life, matter and energy. They embody Air Liquide’s scientific territory and have been at the core of the company’s activities since its creation in 1902.

We welcome and consider applications from all qualified applicants, regardless of their background. We strongly believe a diverse organization opens up opportunities for people to express their talent, both individually and collectively and it helps foster our ability to innovate by living our fundamentals, acting for our success and creating an engaging environment in a changing world.

title: Workplace Business Partner
description:
Workplace Business Partner

The Opportunity

Adobe is working in a period of swift change fueled by AI, shifting workforce expectations, evolving work patterns, and accelerated business expansion. As the company grows, choices regarding work environment and location need to be more flexible, informed by data, and consistent with business goals.

The Workplace Business Partner (WBP) serves as the strategic link between Workplace Strategy & Site Operations (WSSO) and Adobe's business units, directing the development of workforce-informed location strategies that promote business growth, innovation, collaboration, and employee experience.

This position integrates business collaboration, location strategy, and workplace expertise to make sure workplace investments correspond with shifting business priorities and upcoming ways of working. The Workplace Business Partner is tasked with formulating strategic recommendations, promoting agreement among partners, and representing business priorities during workplace planning, governance, and implementation efforts. Execution is carried out in collaboration with teams throughout WSSO.

As Adobe develops within a technology-enhanced environment, this role predicts shifting business requirements and finds emerging workplace opportunities that foster organizational adaptability and long-term value creation.

What you'll do

The Workplace Business Partner holds responsibility for:

  • Developing business-aligned location strategies and future-state recommendations.
  • Transforming business priorities, workforce trends, and organizational changes into workplace and portfolio investment recommendations.
  • Driving collaborator alignment on strategic workplace and location decisions.
  • Establishing success criteria and targeted business results for workplace initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Business Partnership

  • Build and maintain positive relationships with senior business leaders, HR Business Partners, and key collaborators.
  • Act as the main strategic point of contact between WSSO and designated business organizations.
  • Understand business objectives, workforce strategies, organizational changes, and growth plans to assess implications for workplace, location, and portfolio decisions.
  • Represent business objectives within WSSO and support alignment between organizational needs and workplace priorities.

2. Work Location Approach

  • Conduct external market analysis and benchmarking to inform workforce distribution, evaluate location opportunities, and inform investment considerations.
  • Build strategic recommendations for a workforce-informed location strategy aligned with business objectives.
  • Develop strategic recommendations, and executive presentations for leadership review and approval.

3. Strategic Program Leadership

  • Sponsor and guide workplace initiatives from strategy development through implementation partnering with GSO, GWE, and GWD to ensure business objectives are represented.
  • Partner with functional experts across WSSO who own analytics, planning processes, programs, project delivery, and operations to develop aligned recommendations and drive successful outcomes.
  • Provide business intelligence, workforce planning inputs, collaborator alignment, and strategic recommendations that inform governance and approval processes, including the Global Workplace Approval Committee (GWAC).
  • Identify risks, dependencies, and organizational impacts associated with workplace decisions.
  • Represent designated business units in prioritizing workplace investments among competing organizational demands.

4. Change Management & Collaborator Engagement

  • Lead collaborator engagement efforts related to work location strategy initiatives.
  • Collaborate with Site Operation teams to communicate recommendations, rationale, and encouraged outcomes to business leaders and partners.
  • Support adoption of workplace initiatives through effective communication and change management planning.

5. Key Partnerships

The Workplace Business Partner develops workforce and location strategies that correspond with business needs through close collaboration with:

  • Global Site Operations (GSO) – operational feasibility and site readiness
  • Global Workplace Delivery (GWD) or equivalent experience – real estate strategy and project execution
  • Global Workplace Experience (GWE) – employee experience strategy & workplace build
  • HR Business Partners (HRBP) – perspectives on workforce planning and organizational strategy

What you need to succeed

  • Over 8 years of experience in workplace strategy, corporate real estate, business relationship management, consulting, or long-term business development.
  • Experience formulating workplace, portfolio, or location approaches in a complex global organization.
  • Strong executive presence and ability to influence senior leaders and collaborators.
  • Experience crafting arguments, well-founded proposals, and analyses of return on investment.
  • Strong analytical capabilities with the ability to synthesize data into actionable insights.
  • Excellent communication, facilitation, negotiation, and collaborator management skills.
  • Experience with workplace strategy, corporate real estate, workforce planning, and portfolio management is preferred.
  • Strong understanding of workplace trends, hybrid work models, organizational build, and new technologies impacting the future of work.
  • Ability to develop creative concepts and promoting new ideas
  • Working experience with abstract ideas and future-state planning
  • Experience leading the approach to complex, self-directed assignments
  • Passion for introducing innovative ideas that influence significant business decisions

About Adobe

Adobe empowers everyone to create through innovative platforms and tools that unleash creativity, productivity and personalized customer experiences. Adobe’s industry-leading offerings including Adobe Acrobat Studio, Adobe Express, Adobe Firefly, Creative Cloud, Adobe Experience Platform, Adobe Experience Manager, and GenStudio enable people and businesses to turn ideas into impact, powered by AI and driven by human ingenuity.

Our 30,000+ employees worldwide are creating the future and raising the bar as we drive the next decade of growth. We’re on a mission to hire the very best and believe in creating a company culture where all employees are empowered to make an impact. At Adobe, we believe that great ideas can come from anywhere in the organization. The next big idea could be yours.


Let’s Adobe together

At Adobe, we believe in creating a company culture where all employees are empowered to make an impact. Learn more about Adobe life, including our values and culture, focus on people, purpose and community, Adobe for All, comprehensive benefits programs, the stories we tell, the customers we serve, and how you can help us advance our mission of empowering everyone to create.

Adobe is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on gender, race or color, ethnicity or national origin, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Learn more.

title: CFSD Administrative Officer
description:
IMPORTANT NOTICE: Arlington County requires all applicants to thoroughly complete each section of the application, including prior job responsibilities, duties, and supplemental questions. While you may attach a resume, it will not replace a completed application. Incomplete applications will not be considered.

The Child and Family Services Division (CFSD) of the Department of Human Services (DHS) is seeking an Administrative Officer with strong business acumen and demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with system partners to monitor and administer a budget of almost $25 million. The Administrative Officer is a critical senior leadership position responsible for fiscal stewardship and resource allocation to support an effective service delivery system for children and families.

The Administrative Officer is responsible for monitoring and coordinating all financial processes, human resources, procurement, and general administrative functions for CFSD. This incumbent will lead and manage the work of 8 financial and administrative staff and provide direct supervision to four staff. A primary focus of this position is extensive management analysis in support of the Division’s mission to provide excellent innovative services that promote safety, protect children, and preserve and strengthen families.

Specific duties include:

  • Directing budget formulation, financial management, and procurement processes to ensure compliance with local, state, and federal regulations;
  • Monitoring program audits and grants management;
  • Tracking personnel transactions and expenditures to support revenue maximization and monitor state-reimbursable positions;
  • Reconciling accounts and initiating journal entries, budget revisions, and other fiscal adjustments;
  • Supervising staff directly and indirectly, including hiring, training, assigning work, evaluating performance, and coordinating disciplinary actions;
  • Managing contracts by writing specifications, negotiating pricing, monitoring performance, and evaluating program effectiveness;
  • Leading the development and oversight of Children’s Services Act (CSA) programming across multiple child-serving agencies;
  • Participating as a senior leader on Family Assessment and Planning and Community Management and Planning Teams;
  • Developing policies, procedures, and performance measurement systems to support quality improvement, board reporting, and compliance initiatives; and
  • Collaborating with DHS stakeholders and senior management to guide strategic planning, training, and cross-agency coordination for children and family services.

Arlington County DHS is committed to delivering client services in an effective, equitable, respectful, and trauma-informed manner. Our staff is dedicated to ensuring our clients are approached, engaged and cared for in ways that demonstrate competency, sensitivity and awareness of factors which impact the client experience. This includes but is not limited to: cultural identity, gender, racial, and ethnic diversity, religious/spiritual ascription, physical capability, cognitive and literacy levels, sexual orientation, and linguistic needs.

Minimum requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business/Public Administration or related field; and
  • Significant and progressively responsible full-time experience in program administration and/or management, which includes budget development and analysis, and/or reconciliation of accounts, and other administrative functions such as Human Resources, Procurement, program planning, grants management, and/or contracts management.

Substitution: Additional education may be substituted for experience. Additional experience may be substituted for education.

Desirable: Preference may be given to candidates with experience or proficiency in one or more of the following:

  • Policy analysis, program evaluation, and performance measurement;
  • Navigating local government programs involving State and Federal funding and associated accountability;
  • Software tools including word processing, spreadsheets, databases, and presentation platforms; and/or
  • Interpreting procurement regulations, managing HR policies or systems, and coordinating cross-functional teams or stakeholders.

Special Requirements

Background Check: A pre-employment criminal records check will be conducted. It will include checks of the following: criminal record, driving record, education, professional licensure, and credit history. You will be required to sign a release authorizing the County to obtain your background information.

Driver’s License: The applicant must possess, or obtain by the time of appointment, a valid motor vehicle operator's license from the applicant's place of residence or commit to utilizing alternate means of transportation to perform assigned duties and responsibilities at locations other than the primary worksite. If the applicant possesses or acquires a license, the applicant must authorize Arlington County to obtain, or the applicant must provide a copy of the applicant's official state/district driving record. Any offer of employment may be contingent upon a favorable review of the applicant's driving record.[WJ1.1]

Additional Information

Work Hours: 8:00 am to 5:00 pm., Monday through Friday with occasional evening meetings scheduled in advance and weekend preparation. Some telework is available.

Own the technical backbone behind one of the most significant supply chain transformations in Australian retail.

MECCA is building a new Distribution Centre and continuing to evolve the technology that powers its warehouse, fulfilment and supply chain operations. We’re looking for a Technical Lead to take ownership of the supply chain systems landscape — leading a small systems engineering team, getting close to live warehouse operations, and helping MECCA build stronger internal capability across its WMS, codebase, releases and operational support model.

Career-defining transformation exposure - play a key technical leadership role as MECCA brings a new DC and next-generation supply chain capability online

Critical platform ownership - take ownership of the systems that keep warehouse, fulfilment and transport operations moving

Tier-one WMS environment - work across Blue Yonder and a broader warehouse technology landscape

Real engineering influence - help MECCA mature code ownership, pull requests, releases and deployment cadence in-house

Operational impact - work close to the warehouse floor, solving real problems that affect fulfilment, service and customer experience

  • Own codebase management, pull requests, release cadence and deployment practices — reducing dependency on third-party vendors over time

  • Technical ownership experience across warehouse, fulfilment, logistics, supply chain or retail technology environments

  • Experience leading systems engineers, developers or technical support teams in a live operational setting

  • Confidence reviewing code, assessing pull requests, and owning release cadence and codebase governance

  • Strong operational problem-solving skills, comfortable working directly with warehouse, service desk and technology stakeholders

Nice to have:

No exact Blue Yonder background? If you’ve owned a comparable tier-one WMS or complex warehouse technology environment and can work across Java, JavaScript and SQL Server, we’d still be keen to talk.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role with a strong operational lens. If you enjoy owning systems end to end, getting close to the business, improving engineering practices and leading through real-world operational complexity, we’d love to hear from you.

Your Life At MECCA

outputs align with design specifications. o Record data and performance metrics to analyze the effectiveness of engineering operations and identify areas for improvement. o Provide feedback to engineering teams based on test results and system evaluations, focusing on enhancing output quality and efficiency. • Maintenance & Equipment Support: o Assist in the setup, maintenance, and repair of engineering equipment and systems to ensure continuous production and optimized outputs. o Conduct preventive maintenance checks to avoid unplanned downtime and ensure consistent output levels. o Work closely with engineering teams to identify improvements in equipment and system designs to enhance production outputs. • Process Improvement & Troubleshooting: o Identify inefficiencies and engineering changes and upgrades to improve system performance and output. • Documentation & Reporting: o Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of engineering activities, test results, and output data. o Report on system performance, issues, and improvements related to engineering operations, focusing on output efficiency. o Provide detailed reports to management about the status of engineering projects and production outputs. • Collaboration with Cross-Functional Teams: o Work closely with production, quality assurance, and other cross-functional teams to align on production schedules and output targets. o Support engineers in the development of process and equipment specifications to meet output requirements. o Ensure seamless coordination between engineering and other departments to prevent delays in meeting output goals. title: Systems Engineer - Mid to Expert Level (Maryland)
description:
As a System Engineer, you will apply your expertise to develop and improve systems and tools that enable intelligence operations, upholding rigorous engineering and scientific standards. With opportunities spanning cybersecurity, engineering, computer science, and more, you will utilize your skills to drive innovation and make a meaningful impact in protecting the nation.

As a Systems Engineer (SE) with the National Security Agency, you will help shape the future of national security systems by designing, integrating, and optimizing complex technologies that directly affect mission outcomes. In this challenging environment, innovation and critical thinking are essential as you work to safeguard the nation's most sensitive information through cutting edge solutions. Our SEs collaborate with system architects, mission customers, and key stakeholders to guide technical direction, ensuring projects meet operational requirements and align with strategic priorities. Key responsibilities include: - System Design and Integration: Spearhead the development of system architectures, ensuring seamless integration and functionality across diverse platforms. - Project Leadership: Lead cross-functional teams through the full project lifecycle, from concept through delivery. You will manage project timelines, budgets, and quality metrics to ensure mission success. - Technical Oversight: Provide expert guidance on technical issues and oversee the implementation of engineering best practices to enhance system reliability and performance. - Risk Management: Identify and mitigate technical risks through thorough analysis and proactive planning. Your insights will be crucial in maintaining the resiliency of our systems. - Mentoring and Collaboration: Foster a collaborative and continuous improvement environment through mentoring junior engineers and promoting knowledge-sharing within the team. Valuable expertise in fields like cybersecurity, SIGINT, electrical or computer engineering, physics, computer science, machine learning, artificial intelligence, network architecture, IT infrastructure, and hybrid communications will be leveraged to drive the development of next-generation technologies, tackling the nation's toughest challenges and supporting NSA's global mission. Risk and mitigation management is also a critical aspect for our system engineers who will have oversight on system security, particularly in a Zero Trust environment, reliability, resiliency, data integrity, compliance, regulations, operational efficiency, and user experience. By maintaining oversight on these areas, System Engineers can significantly reduce risks and ensure the reliability, security, and efficiency of the systems they manage. MID-CAREER SYSTEMS ENGINEERS Mid-career systems engineers have experience leading systems engineering efforts and are ready to apply or expand that knowledge within the Intelligence Community. These engineers have experience in specific lifecycle phases, as well as an understanding of the full lifecycle. They develop their expertise, grow their breadth of knowledge, and mentor the next generation of systems engineers. Mid-career systems engineers come from a wide variety of experiences such as Cybersecurity, SIGINT, telecommunications, and systems of systems or networking infrastructure. These professionals are adept at communicating with technical teams and making recommendations to senior leadership that drive mission initiatives. They collaborate with senior engineers on system integration and testing, and develop and maintain technical documentation. SENIOR SYSTEMS ENGINEERS Seasoned professionals drive the Agency's largest and most challenging technical projects to ensure success. These engineers participate in technical decision-making or function in an advisory role. Working in collaborative teams, they lead technical teams and define and manage technical requirements throughout the product lifecycle. They identify and manage technical program risk; evaluate architectural design for efficiency improvements; and capture, analyze, and recommend updates to the enterprise and mission architectures to ensure resiliency. Senior Systems Engineers design and implement large-scale systems and architectures, and oversee system integration and testing. They develop and maintain technical roadmaps and strategies, while understanding the technical implications of different design choices and architectural decisions. Staying up-to-date with industry trends, emerging technologies, and best practices, Senior Systems Engineers provide technical guidance and oversight to ensure that systems are designed and built to meet business and operational requirements. They identify potential technical risks and opportunities, and mentor other systems engineers in their tradecraft, laying the foundation for future successes.

The Role + Purpose:

Collaborate with Merchants and Allocators on preseason and in season plans to align on sales and inventory strategies. Provide team with diagnosis of the business and own suggested course of action.

PRESEASON

  • Create preseason sales, margin and inventory plans by department, class, style, and color. Analyze and report on previous quarter results; identify “missed sales” and growth drivers over prior year

IN SEASON

Benefits Strategy & Program Management

We’re uniting science, technology, and talent to get ahead of disease together.


Find out more: Our approach to R&D

Job Purpose

Are you energized by a medical writing and submissions role that allows you to shape clinical document strategy and accelerate product approvals? If so, this Director Medical Writing Asset Lead role could be an exciting opportunity to consider.

As Medical Writing Asset Lead Director, you will apply experience, scientific and operational expertise, and leadership in a matrix organization to provide the medical writing and submissions strategy for one or more assets (main asset Hepatology.) You will design and deliver high-quality fit for purpose clinical documents for global regulatory submissions, plan for efficient and accelerated ways of working, and contribute to key organizational process improvements.

This is a highly visible medical writing role, that will provide YOU the opportunity to lead key activities to progress YOUR career.

We encourage you to bring your disruptive thinking, collaborative spirit, and diverse perspective to our organization.

Key responsibilities:

These responsibilities include some of the following:

  • Providing key contributions to clinical document strategy for one or more assets throughout the life cycle of drug development. Documents in scope include but are not limited to clinical study protocols, clinical sections of the IMPD/IND, investigator brochures, clinical study reports, briefing documents for regulatory authorities, Common Technical Document Summaries and Clinical Overview, and responses to regulatory authority questions.

  • Leading matrix teams in planning and production of multiple clinical documents, working with CROs and/or independent contractors as needed.

  • Planning and successfully delivering large submissions independently, effectively recommending innovative methods and solutions for achieving accelerated timelines. Assessing and adapting to interdependences of various contributing functions and managing problems affecting timelines as necessary. Ensuring a global approach for submissions as appropriate, collaborating with Global Regulatory Affairs to ensure business needs and regulatory requirements are met. Providing guidance and facilitation to submission teams in development of detailed submission plans.

  • Acting as lead author on submissions. Effectively organizing content and arguments in complex clinical submission documents, including briefing documents and responses to regulatory questions.

  • Proposing resourcing solutions for major projects including the number of FTEs required and best use of internal and external resources.

  • Actively contributing to development of training materials for therapeutic area and providing mentoring and/or training on regulatory requirements, medical writing processes, and submission planning to individuals or teams.

  • Driving, promoting and implementing key organizational process improvement initiatives. Proactively generating ideas for simplification and improvement taking advantage of opportunities that arise and challenging the status quo. Incorporating, promoting and encouraging the adoption of technology for clinical documents within medical writing and the stakeholder landscape.

  • Prioritizing and meeting multiple deadlines successfully with attention to detail, demonstrating high performance standards for own work and encouraging similar standards across the matrix.

  • Promoting leadership behaviors that support GSK values.

Why you?

Basic Qualifications:

We are looking for professionals with these required skills to achieve our goals:

  • PhD, PharmD, MPH, MSc, or other post-graduate degree

  • Substantial experience in clinical regulatory writing and regulatory submissions in the pharmaceutical industry, with a proven track record of writing the clinical documents in scope.

  • Strong experience in project management, planning, communication, and demonstrated matrix leadership to deliver results

Preferred Qualifications:

If you have the following characteristics, it would be a plus:

  • Experience in delivering accelerated submissions for EU, US, China, Japan and Rest of World.

  • Experience in Hepatology therapy area.

  • Demonstrated cross-functional collaborator with effective communication skills and experience in building networks and influencing partners and stakeholders at all levels of the organization.

  • Excellent understanding of clinical operations / medical writing processes, and ICH/GCP and global regulatory guidelines for drug development and approval.

  • Strong strategic and critical thinking, problem solving, influencing and decision-making capabilities.


Working arrangements
This role has a hybrid working model. You will work on-site 2/3 days per week as agreed with your manager to support collaboration and team needs.


Skills

Clinical Development, Clinical Trial Designs, Communication, Customer Service, Decision Making, Emotional Intelligence, Influencing Without Authority, Learning Agility, Literature Reviews, Medical Writing, Pharmaceutical Industry, Presentation Techniques, Regulatory Submissions, Scientific Writing, Strategic Thinking

Why GSK?

Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.

GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.

People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. title: Senior UI/UX Designer
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior UI/UX Designer based in Canada.

This is a high-impact design role focused on building and scaling a unified design system across a global SaaS product portfolio. You will combine hands-on design expertise with strategic influence, creating reusable components, design tokens, interaction patterns, and accessibility standards. Working closely with product designers and front-end engineers, you will help bridge the gap between design and implementation. You will also establish governance, documentation, and contribution practices that enable teams to work consistently and efficiently. The role offers the opportunity to shape design quality across multiple products while mentoring other designers and influencing technical and product decisions. You’ll join a distributed, collaborative environment that values autonomy, continuous learning, and thoughtful design.

Accountabilities:

  • Own the end-to-end design and continuous evolution of the design system, covering foundations such as color, typography, spacing, iconography, motion, and complex interactive components.
  • Build and maintain a scalable design-token architecture that connects design libraries with front-end implementation and promotes consistency across products.
  • Define and document component specifications, usage guidelines, interaction patterns, accessibility requirements, and design rationale so engineering teams can implement solutions effectively.
  • Partner closely with front-end engineers to develop reusable components that meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards and align with modern component-based technologies.
  • Audit existing product interfaces, identify inconsistencies, create component inventories, and establish prioritized roadmaps for design-system coverage and improvement.
  • Collaborate with product designers across multiple teams to understand requirements, validate new patterns, and ensure the design system evolves around real product needs.
  • Establish and maintain governance practices covering contributions, versioning, deprecation, change management, and communication to keep the system scalable and trusted.
  • Champion accessibility and inclusive design by embedding accessible patterns directly into system components and design specifications.
  • Drive adoption through enablement sessions, Figma documentation, guidance, and ongoing support for designers and developers.
  • Contribute to the development of the design-systems function by mentoring junior designers, supporting hiring decisions, and helping define how design quality and system effectiveness are measured.

    • Requirements:

    • 5–8 years of UX/UI design experience, including at least 3 years focused on design systems or design infrastructure, preferably within B2B SaaS or enterprise software.
    • Demonstrated experience creating and scaling design systems, including component libraries, design tokens, contribution models, and governance frameworks.
    • Expert proficiency with Figma, including component variants, Auto Layout, Variables/design tokens, interactive prototyping, and library management.
    • Strong understanding of front-end implementation constraints and the ability to collaborate effectively with engineers using HTML, CSS, and component-based frameworks such as React, Angular, or Web Components.
    • Practical knowledge of WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards and experience embedding accessible design patterns into components from the specification stage.
    • Experience establishing design-system governance, including versioning, deprecation workflows, contribution guidelines, and change communication.
    • Strong documentation skills, with the ability to translate design intent into clear usage guidelines, annotated specifications, and decision rationale for engineering teams.
    • Experience conducting UI audits, creating component inventories, and developing prioritized design-system roadmaps aligned with product and business objectives.
    • Excellent collaboration and influencing skills, with the ability to align designers and engineers around design-system decisions without relying on formal authority.
    • Comfortable working with globally distributed teams across different time zones, working styles, and levels of design maturity.
    • A degree in Interaction Design, Graphic Design, Human-Computer Interaction, or a related discipline is preferred; equivalent professional experience will also be considered.
    • Strong communication, mentoring, problem-solving, and stakeholder-management abilities, with a proactive and systems-oriented approach.

      • Benefits:

      • Remote-first flexibility with the opportunity to work from Brazil, United States or Canada.
      • Full-time permanent employment with a global, distributed team.
      • Competitive compensation, with the advertised range of $50,000–$145,000 USD depending on location, experience, and qualifications; local compensation details may apply.
      • Potential eligibility for additional compensation, including bonuses or commissions.
      • Comprehensive benefits package, subject to location and employment terms.
      • Opportunity to work on a global SaaS product portfolio and influence design standards across multiple products.
      • Strong opportunities for professional growth, mentoring, and leadership development.
      • Collaborative culture emphasizing autonomy, flexibility, inclusion, learning, and continuous improvement.
      • Opportunity to shape and grow a design-systems function with broad organizational impact.

title: 6-Month Internship - Supply, Trading & Shipping - Singapore (Jan - Jun 2027)
description:
Entity:

Supply, Trading & Shipping


Job Family Group:

Business Support Group, Supply & Trading Group


Job Description:

bp supply, trading & shipping 6-month internship programme (Jan - Jun 2027)

About bp

As a leading global energy company with a presence in 61 countries, bp’s purpose is to deliver energy to the world, today and tomorrow. We are one of only a few companies that can deliver energy – at scale – to countries and millions of customers every day. With more than 100 years of experience, we bring together technology, innovation and deep expertise that keeps communities moving – and we’re still evolving.

About early careers

Early careers opportunities

Your talent. Your skills. Your big ideas (and even bigger dreams). We know you have a lot to give. So we’ll make sure you get a lot in return. From next-level experiences to global impact. From inspiring teammates to exceptional support – we offer graduate and internship roles across multiple areas.

Our internships

Make an impact on cutting-edge projects. Help find solutions to complex challenges. Be part of a company that invests in you and your growth. You can do it all as an intern at bp. Our 6-month internship programme gives you the opportunity to build your technical knowledge, develop key skills and learn more about life at bp. You'll be part of one team throughout your internship, supported by a dedicated line manager and buddy. There’ll be opportunities to connect with other interns, take part in training and grow your network across the business.

Role and Responsibilities

The internship programme is designed to give you maximum exposure to our supply, trading & shipping business. You will be working on projects with real impact to our business. You’ll be placed in a team with opportunities to showcase and enhance your skillset, follow your ambition and be part of the team’s success.

Examples of previous projects include:

  • Carrying out research and analysis into a particular market or new jurisdiction and producing a strategy to help support trading decisions and growth.

  • Producing daily news/customer information reports to highlight market information and opportunities for trading and origination.

  • Analytics in support of our fundamental and demand supply view for short/medium term revenue activity.

  • Working to automate and optimise systems, reports, and analysis to speed up trading processes and decisions using various data science techniques.

Over the course of the internship programme, you’ll have the opportunity to learn about our graduate programme through networking, training & information sessions before deciding on which graduate development track you would like to be considered for as our summer internship is a primary pipeline for our 2028 supply, trading and shipping graduate programme.

Supply, trading & shipping development tracks include:

Trading: Joining our energy trading team, you’ll be part of managing our trades on all the major energy commodity exchanges and the OTC market as well as our daily exposure. You’ll have the opportunity to experience different trading disciplines and styles from physical trading to paper trading.

Analytics: Analysts have the opportunity to directly influence trading decisions as part of a highly commercial and skilled team. Working in the fast-paced environment of our trading floors and with access to vast amounts of data and information, you’ll focus on driving continued growth in trading profits and acting as a subject matter expert on energy market fundamentals.

Commercial: Every year, bp invests billions of dollars searching for new sources of energy, supplying our customers with the fuels they need. You’ll help to ensure we make the best use of our investment. We want you to be in the best position to propose new and creative ways to maximize value. There are many commercial teams responsible for building and maintaining key relationships, developing unique solutions to address bp’s and our customer’s business needs and creating additional value for our trading business.

About you ​

You’ll have strong organizational skills and the ability to deliver results in a collaborative environment. Your agility to learn and adapt will be key along with the energy, motivation, and ownership to make the most of this fantastic opportunity. You’ll be comfortable making courageous and bold decisions, have digital fluency, a keen eye for analytics and the insights they provide.

Even though good levels of numeracy are important, you won’t necessarily need a formal technical background. You’ll bring well-rounded life experience, and your strong academic results will be supported by some work experience, everything from customer service to industry experience is great!

We know you’re early in your career – we don’t expect you to be an expert.

To be eligible for the ST&S internship programme you are:

  • currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in any discipline which could range from Business, Commerce, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Arts to STEM

  • in your penultimate year of study, graduating between December 2027 and July 2028

  • on track to achieve a cumulative GPA equivalent to Second Upper Honours or above

  • a Singapore citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident with the rights to work in Singapore

Please note the following when applying:

  • You can only apply to 1 bp early careers opportunity globally per academic year – within this time, we will only process the first application you make, and you’ll be withdrawn from any subsequent applications.

  • Please note that vacancies are filled on an ongoing basis after opening and we may close applications before any stated deadline. Therefore, we highly recommend you submit your application as early as possible to be considered for the opportunity of your choice.

Applications close on 25 September 2026.


Travel Requirement

No travel is expected with this role


Relocation Assistance:

This role is not eligible for relocation


Remote Type:

This position is not available for remote working


Skills:

Adaptability, Authenticity, Communication, Continuous Learning, Courage, Creativity and Innovation, Curiosity, Decision Making, Digital Fluency, Ethical judgement, Excellence, Group Problem Solving, Influencing, Knowledge Sharing, Listening, Managing volatility, Resilience, Self-Awareness, Stakeholder Engagement, Stakeholder Management, Understanding Emotions, Writing skills

title: Psychology Program Manager
description:
The Psychology Program Manager is assigned to the Mental Illness Research Education and Clinical Center (MIRECC) at the VA Maryland Health Care System (VAMHCS). The Program Manager/Consultant serves the VA Psychosocial Rehabilitation Program (VA PRT) that currently oversees the national VA roll-out the VA Social Skills (VA SST) Training Program. The position will be based at the Baltimore Division of the VAMHCS, but may require work at other VAMHCS or VISN sites.

Duties: Responsible for coordinating, implementing, maintaining, evaluating, and managing programmatic aspects of the large-scale, national competency-based training programs. Responsibilities include oversight of teaching/training, program evaluation, and administrative activities for the VA Social Skills Training Training Program which includes multiple national VA-SST Regional Trainers across all VISNs as well as a small staff of national SST training and administrative staff. Oversees the initial and ongoing training and development of the VA national and regional SST training staff. Oversees the development and management of VA-SST program budgets and related resource utilization. Identifies program problems and the negotiation of corrective action concerning programmatic issues and basic financial management of the program as well as the application of clinical and administrative knowledge in identification, analysis, and resolution of issues pertaining to the quality of mental health care. Develops and maintains a system of ongoing measurement of program accomplishments (program goals and objectives) and program outcomes using a data-driven quality assurance process of a program that delivers specialized, complex, highly professional services that are important program components. Develops training modules, resources, and materials to support operation of the VA-SST training program. Works individually and in collaboration with others, responsible for the preparation of issue briefs on key aspects of the VASST program and is responsible for direct communication regarding program accomplishments with leadership at the local and national VA levels. Maintains communication with mental health professionals working in the field for VHA with regard to VA-SST technical assistance initiatives and programs and ensuring that technical requirements. Responsible for delivery of expert assistance in support of the VA-SST program to wide variety of professional audiences and serves as point of contact for dissemination of information to a broad group of stakeholders. Promotes the highest possible quality of care for VA patients seeking treatment and services throughout their VA medical systems through planning, development, and implementation of the SST program to meet the needs of Veterans by facilitating the improvement of quality and availability of treatment, prevention, and rehabilitation services in order to reduce illness, death, and cost. Works with appropriate staff in the Institute for Learning, Education and Development (ILEAD) and VISNs and with staff in OMH and others in Patient Care Services to identify VA-SST training needs, develop appropriate training modules, and accomplish educational requirements for staff. Participates in local and national workgroups to further the progress of evidence-based clinician training initiatives. Responsible for strategic planning to ensure the provision of high-quality services to meet the needs of the Veterans being served and planning, developing, and implementing short- and long-term goals and objectives consistent with the section's strategic plan. Performs other duties as requested or assigned. Total Rewards of a Allied Health Professional Work Schedule: 8:00am-4:30pm, Monday-Friday Compressed/Flexible: Not Available Recruitment/Relocation Incentives (Sign-on Bonus): Not Authorized Permanent Change of Station (Relocation Assistance): Not Authorized Pay: Competitive salary and regular salary increases. When setting pay, a higher step rate of the appropriate grade may be determined after consideration of higher or unique qualifications or special needs of the VA (Above Minimum Rate of the Grade). Paid Time Off: 37-50 days of annual paid time offer per year (13-26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year). Selected applicants may qualify for credit toward annual leave accrual, based on prior [work experience] or military service experience. Parental Leave: After 12 months of employment, up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave in connection with the birth, adoption, or foster care placement of a child. Child Care Subsidy: After 60 days of employment, full time employees with a total family income below $144,000 may be eligible for a childcare subsidy up to 25% of total eligible childcare costs for eligible children up to the monthly maximum of $416.66. Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Telework: Available; Ad-hoc Virtual: This is not a virtual position. Functional Statement #: 260439F Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not Authorized

title: JIRA Developer
description:
Our Company

EOS IT Solutions is a global technology and logistics company, providing Collaboration and Business IT Support services to some of the world's largest industry leaders. We deliver innovative solutions that simplify complex technology challenges, enabling our customers to focus on their core business objectives.
At EOS, we are committed to excellence, innovation and continuous improvement. Our people are at the centre of everything we do, and we foster a collaborative environment where diverse perspectives and ideas are valued.

Position Overview

We are seeking a skilled Jira Developer to design, develop and optimise Jira-based solutions that support business processes across the organisation. The successful candidate will work closely with technical and business stakeholders to customise Jira and associated Atlassian products, build integrations, automate workflows and enhance the overall user experience.
This role requires strong technical expertise, problem-solving skills and a passion for delivering scalable and efficient solutions that drive business value.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, develop and maintain custom Jira solutions, workflows, screens, fields and permissions.
  • Configure and administer Jira Software, Jira Service Management and other Atlassian tools as required.
  • Develop and maintain integrations between Jira and third-party applications using REST APIs and other integration technologies.
  • Create automation rules and scripts to improve operational efficiency and user productivity.
  • Collaborate with business stakeholders to gather requirements and translate them into technical solutions.
  • Troubleshoot, diagnose and resolve Jira platform issues and performance bottlenecks.
  • Develop custom plugins, extensions or applications where standard Jira functionality does not meet business needs.
  • Support platform upgrades, migrations and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Maintain technical documentation, system configurations and development standards.
  • Ensure solutions align with security, compliance and governance requirements.
  • Provide guidance and best practices to users and project teams on Jira capabilities and functionality.
  • Participate in code reviews, testing and quality assurance activities.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience developing and administering Jira within enterprise environments.
  • Strong knowledge of Jira Software, Jira Service Management and Atlassian ecosystem tools.
  • Experience working with Jira APIs, automation frameworks and scripting tools.
  • Proficiency in one or more programming languages such as Java, Groovy, JavaScript or Python.
  • Experience with REST APIs, web services and systems integration.
  • Understanding of Agile methodologies, Scrum and DevOps practices.
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management capabilities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Atlassian certifications (e.g. ACP certifications).
  • Experience developing Jira plugins using Atlassian SDK.
  • Experience with Confluence administration and integration.
  • Familiarity with cloud and enterprise infrastructure environments.
  • Knowledge of CI/CD tools and integration platforms.
  • Experience supporting large-scale global user communities.

What Success Looks Like

  • Jira solutions are reliable, scalable and aligned to business requirements.
  • Workflows and automations improve operational efficiency and user experience.
  • Integrations perform consistently and securely across platforms.
  • Stakeholders receive responsive support and trusted technical guidance.
  • Platform governance, security and documentation standards are maintained.

Skills and Competencies

  • Customer-focused mindset
  • Strong collaboration and teamwork
  • Continuous improvement approach
  • Effective prioritisation and organisation
  • Technical innovation and creativity
  • Attention to detail
  • Ownership and accountability
  • Adaptability in a dynamic environment

Why Join EOS?

  • Opportunity to work on innovative technology solutions at global scale.
  • Collaborative and inclusive culture that values diverse perspectives.
  • Professional development and career growth opportunities.
  • Exposure to cutting-edge technologies and enterprise platforms.
  • Flexible and supportive working environment.

Belonging at EOS

EOS is committed to creating a diverse, equitable and inclusive workplace where everyone feels respected, valued and empowered to succeed. We believe that a variety of backgrounds, experiences and perspectives strengthens our teams and drives innovation.
We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and are dedicated to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process. If you require support or adjustments, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

title: Cloud Solutions Engineer
description:
The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

Information Systems and Cyber Division (ISCD) staff couple the latest in information system technologies, such as elastic compute clouds, containerization, microservices, real-time operating systems, and visualization frameworks, with expertise in cyber security, software architecture, software engineering, process improvement, and software development to deliver responsive, resilient, high-performance software intensive systems to our Intelligence Community (IC), Department of Defense (DoD), and civilian customers.

The Cloud Platforms and Architectures Department (CPAD) goes beyond traditional software systems design and IT application hosting environments. We provide our customers with guidance and solutions for developing, deploying, and managing cloud software systems that are highly secure, available, resilient, and scalable. We are looking for a Cloud Solutions Engineer to contribute to the delivery of these services. If you’re a passionate and driven individual who is excited about developing advanced cloud solutions that keep our nation at the forefront of space systems capabilities, consider joining our team of talented engineers.

Work Model

This is a full-time position that will require 5 days/week onsite work in Chantilly, VA.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Providing cloud subject matter expertise to DoD, IC, and Civil Space customers
  • Developing proof-of-concept prototypes to help customers understand the latest cloud technologies
  • Designing and implementing cloud-based solutions to meet customer and mission needs
  • Providing guidance on reference cloud architectures and best practices for the space enterprise
  • Conducting cloud architecture reviews of customer mission systems
  • Conducting research of tools and cloud services to inform stakeholders of ideal or alternative solutions
  • Growing departmental knowledge through work, training assignments, and presentations

What You Need to be Successful – Engineering Specialist

Minimum Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in STEM, with an emphasis in Computer Science or other related sciences/engineering discipline
  • 7 or more years of relevant experience with designing and implementing cloud-based systems to meet business or mission needs
  • Proven experience with Azure cloud technologies
  • Experience with DevOps tools and practices (e.g. Jenkins, Argo)
  • Familiarity with containerization technologies (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes)
  • Familiarity with cloud security concepts (e.g., network security, identity and access management)
  • Proficient in at least one programming language such as Python or Go
  • Ability to collaborate and communicate effectively in a cross-functional matrix organization
  • Active TS/SCI clearance issued by the U.S. Government, with ability to obtain SAP

How You Can Stand Out

It would be impressive if you have one or more of these:

  • Advanced degree in Computer Science or other sciences/engineering discipline

title: Computer and System Engineer
description:
Employer: Bench Mark IT Services

Job Title: Computer and Systems Engineer

Job Type: Full-time / Permanent

Experience: Minimum 1 year of relevant experience

Work Authorisation: Applicants must have, or be eligible to obtain, the right to work in Australia

Location: Burwood VIC 3125

Salary: $80,000.00 + Superannuation

Job Summary:

We are seeking a skilled and detail-oriented Computer and Systems Engineer to join our IT infrastructure team. The successful candidate will be responsible for analysing, designing, implementing, maintaining, and supporting computer systems, networks, and related infrastructure to meet the operational requirements of the organisation.

The role involves both hardware and software engineering responsibilities, with a strong focus on system reliability, security, performance, scalability, and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Analyse business and technical requirements and design effective computer and systems solutions.
  2. Design, install, configure, test, maintain, and troubleshoot computer systems, servers, operating systems, networks, and related infrastructure.
  3. Install, configure, maintain, and support operating systems and application software across Windows, Linux, UNIX, and macOS environments.
  4. Monitor system performance, availability, capacity, and reliability and identify opportunities for improvement.
  5. Diagnose and resolve system, hardware, software, network, and infrastructure-related issues.
  6. Configure and administer servers, virtual machines, storage systems, and associated infrastructure.
  7. Manage user accounts, permissions, group policies, and system access through Active Directory and related identity-management systems.
  8. Configure and maintain networking services, including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, routing, switching, VPNs, and network security controls.
  9. Implement and maintain cybersecurity measures, including firewalls, endpoint protection, access controls, system hardening, vulnerability management, and security patches.
  10. Develop and maintain backup, recovery, disaster-recovery, and business-continuity procedures.
  11. Administer and support virtualisation technologies, including VMware and Hyper-V.
  12. Configure and support cloud-based infrastructure and services using platforms such as Microsoft Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud Platform.
  13. Automate routine system administration and infrastructure tasks using scripting languages such as PowerShell, Bash, or Python.
  14. Conduct system testing, performance analysis, troubleshooting, and technical investigations.
  15. Assess existing systems and recommend upgrades, replacements, or improvements to enhance efficiency, security, and scalability.
  16. Assist with planning and implementing system migrations, upgrades, integrations, and infrastructure projects.
  17. Maintain accurate technical documentation, including system configurations, architecture diagrams, procedures, service records, and troubleshooting guides.
  18. Liaise and collaborate with developers, network engineers, IT support staff, vendors, and other stakeholders to ensure reliable operation of IT systems.
  19. Evaluate emerging technologies, software, hardware, and infrastructure solutions and provide recommendations to management.
  20. Ensure IT systems and infrastructure comply with organisational policies, security requirements, and relevant industry standards.

Required Skills & Experience

  1. Minimum 1 year of relevant experience in systems engineering, computer systems, network engineering, IT infrastructure, or a closely related role.
  2. Strong knowledge of Windows, Linux, UNIX, and/or macOS operating environments.
  3. Sound understanding of networking concepts and technologies, including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, routing, switching, VPNs, and firewalls.
  4. Experience with Active Directory, Group Policy, user access management, and system administration.
  5. Experience with virtualisation technologies such as VMware and Hyper-V.
  6. Familiarity with cloud platforms such as Microsoft Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud Platform.
  7. Experience with system monitoring, backup, recovery, patching, and security-management tools.
  8. Proficiency in scripting or automation using PowerShell, Bash, Python, or similar technologies.
  9. Good understanding of cybersecurity principles, system hardening, access controls, vulnerability management, and data protection.
  10. Ability to diagnose and resolve complex hardware, software, network, and system issues.
  11. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
  12. Excellent attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate technical documentation.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Computer Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related discipline.
  2. Relevant professional certifications are highly regarded, including:
    • CompTIA Network+ or Security+
    • Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate
    • AWS Certified Solutions Architect or SysOps Administrator
    • Cisco CCNA
    • Red Hat Certified System Administrator (RHCSA)
    • VMware certification or equivalent

Personal Attributes

  1. Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  2. Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
  3. Strong organisational and time-management skills.
  4. Ability to prioritise and manage multiple technical tasks and projects.
  5. A proactive approach to identifying and resolving technical problems.
  6. Commitment to maintaining system security, reliability, and service quality.
  7. Willingness to continuously develop technical knowledge and remain updated with emerging technologies and industry developments.

What We Offer

  1. Full-time permanent employment.
  2. Competitive salary plus superannuation.
  3. Opportunity to work with modern systems, infrastructure, and cloud technologies.
  4. Professional development and career-growth opportunities.
  5. Supportive and collaborative working environment.
  6. Exposure to a broad range of systems engineering and infrastructure projects.

How to Apply

Interested applicants are invited to submit their current resume/CV and a brief cover letter outlining their relevant qualifications, skills, and experience.

Only applicants who meet the requirements of the position will be considered. Shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.

Applications from suitably qualified candidates are encouraged.

Position Description:

The Clinical Trials Unit, provides regulatory support and oversight to key research programs at the University of Louisville. The Research Regulations Specialist II is responsible for preparing research submissions to the IRB of record in a manner that demonstrates understanding and application of the federal regulations governing human subjects in research (i.e.. 45 CFR 46, 21 CFR 50, 56, 312, 812, ICH GCP, and HIPAA). This individual will advise investigators on compliance and research logistics and planning.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Oversight and management of projects for the entire project period to ensure compliance with all applicable regulations, policies and procedures.

  • Evaluate the protocol and sponsor documents to determine if additional items are needed for IRB/Sponsor approval.

  • Be the liaison with the sponsoring agency for regulatory approvals throughout the life of the project

  • Develop the regulatory and essential documents to be in compliance with the protocol and federal/local and affiliated healthcare provider requirements. Prepare consent and HIPAA documents with appropriate language representing the actual events that will occur as part of the research.

  • Complete the electronic IRB submission, preparing IRB modifications based on analysis of contingencies presented by the committee or the study team, processing sponsor requested changes and modifying regulatory documents accordingly, manage essential documents in accordance with the sponsor, IRB and federal government requirements.

  • Submit amendment and continuing review data on behalf of the Principal Investigator, investigate study irregularities and guide staff in reporting and documentation of events.

  • Submit studies for closure and resolve any outstanding relevant findings with the study team.

  • Responsible for quality assurance for regulatory submissions for CTU and other departments. Conduct periodic assessments of submissions to identify exceptions in a timely manner. Oversee all federal and locally required regulatory documentation in a regulatory binder for each protocol. Participate in site qualification visits, site initiation visits, monitoring visits and audits conducted by sponsor, FDA, healthcare providers and IRB.

  • Manage special projects as assigned such as representing the Director of Clinical Regulatory Affairs in regulatory matters when needed, proposing corrective actions, policy revisions, data plans, masking plans.

  • Advise investigators on protocols and protocol ideas, on compliance with University policy and related aspects of conduct of clinical research.

  • Educate departmental staff on regulatory affairs and provide guidance for documentation and process.

  • Participate, support, and lead quality improvement projects.

  • Develop and plan for program or protocol specific corrective and preventative action plans.

  • Write reports to internal and external agencies summarizing results of quality audit and compliance review.

title: Histopathology Technician (Advanced IHC)
description:
This Histopathology Technician position is in Pathology and Laboratory Service at the Richmond VA Medical Center, located in Richmond, Virginia. As crucial members of the McGuire VA Pathology and Laboratory Medicine Service, histopathology technicians possess the knowledge and skills to process anatomical tissue and cytological cell samples obtained from the Veteran by a clinician.

The Histopathology Technician at the GS-7 level have a higher level of responsibility for technical oversight and are expected to carry out assigned tasks of considerable difficulty independently. The technician will have the responsibility of performing difficult Histological, Histochemical and Immunohistochemical procedures, as well as developing, modifying, or adapting new staining methods or techniques, improving existing methods as necessary for routine Histotechnology procedures. The technician will be responsible for troubleshooting issues with instruments and resolving problems. This position requires practical knowledge of the anatomic pathology laboratory practice in one or both areas (i.e. Histopathology and Cytology).The duties and responsibilities of the Histopathology Technician includes but are not limited to the following: Identifies and cuts minute pieces of tissue on both Microtome and Microtome Cryostat for rapid frozen sections such as for MOHS Performs specialized, complex double and triple histochemical testing, staining and arduous special staining of tissue samples. Decalcifies tissue by determining the proper solution. Embeds tissue to give proper orientation for diagnostic interpretation. Performs all routine histopathology work; accessioning, processing tissue, embedding, cutting and staining for microscopic examination of tissue. Determines accuracy of staining such as routine and MOHS H&E (hematoxylin and eosin), and specials such as Mason's Trichrome, and immunohistochemistry through analysis of control slides Advises Pathologists and Residents, when asked, in the treatment or staining of certain tissue. Stains frozen sections with H&E immunofluorescent reagents and other immunohistochemical reagents. Investigates, evaluates, and assists with establishing quality control materials for measuring the validity and accuracy of the stain. Routinely performs difficult and complex testing using monoclonal and polyclonal antibodies to detect various antigens on the surface of cells, in the cytoplasm of cells, and in the nucleus, by immunologic techniques. Develops and implements all new staining procedures, including special immunohistochemical and immunoperoxidase procedures using enzymatic methodologies. Performs complex operations, calibrations, troubleshooting and maintenance on all equipment in the section. Assists the prosector/pathologist in the performance of the autopsy. Determines what type of tissue is being cut to obtain the proper thickness required for different tissue and stains. Determines when a complete section has been obtained, with all margins and structures in the block visible. Evaluates specimen type, such as kidney, brain, lung, etc., for testing method appropriateness. Work Schedule: M-F; 6:00am - 2:30pm Compressed/Flexible: Not Available Telework: Not Available Virtual: This is not a virtual position. Functional Statement #: 0000 Relocation/Recruitment Incentives: Not Authorized Financial Disclosure Report: Not required

title: Emergency Management Specialist (Preparedness)
description:
This position is located in FEMA's Region 10 National Preparedness Division, Technological Hazards Branch. The ideal candidate for this position will have experience executing federal regulations, reviewing plans, managing deadlines, developing and conducting emergency management exercises, and improving readiness by coordinating with stakeholders such as Federal, State, and local partners.

What will I do in this position if hired? In this position, you will serve as an Emergency Management Specialist (Preparedness) in Region 10's National Preparedness Division, Technological Hazards Branch providing expert technical assistance and program delivery support. Typical assignments include: Implementing emergency management standards, regulations, practices, training, and procedures to identify, minimize or eliminate hazards and threats with a focus on readiness. Conducting assessments of emergency plans and preparedness policies, procedures, and provides recommendations for inadequate preparedness functional areas. Preparing a variety of reports, information papers, and briefings concerning emergency planning and preparedness practices to gain program support and describe program accountability for all FEMA stakeholders. Developing regional plans to ensure the capability to continue essential functions during all hazards. Evaluating emergency management processes, execution plans, and standard operating procedures for compliance with established emergency management directives, regulations, policies, laws, standards, and guidance. Providing technical advice on emergency planning and preparedness activities associated with natural and/or man-made disasters. What else do I need to know? At FEMA, our mission is to help people before, during and after disasters, and every employee at FEMA has a role in emergency management. Every FEMA employee has regular and recurring emergency management responsibilities, though not every position requires routine deployment to disaster sites. All positions are subject to recall around the clock for emergency management operations, which may require irregular work hours, work at locations other than the official duty station, and may include duties other than those specified in the employee's official position description. Travel requirements in support of emergency operations may be extensive in nature (weeks to months), with little advance notice, and may require employees to relocate to emergency sites with physically austere and operationally challenging conditions. Promotion Potential: Future promotions will be dependent on your ability to perform the duties at a higher level, the continuing need for an employee assigned to the higher level, and administrative approval.

To ensure the accomplishment of our mission, DHS requires every employee to be reliable and trustworthy. To meet those standards, all selected applicants must undergo, successfully pass, and maintain a background investigation for moderate risk as a condition of placement into this position. This may include a credit check after initial job qualifications are determined, a review of financial issues, such as delinquency in the payment of debts, child support and/or tax obligations, as well as certain criminal offenses and illegal use or possession of drugs (please visit: Mythbuster on Federal Hiring Policies for additional information). For more information on background investigations for Federal jobs please visit OPM Investigations. The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) must authorize employment offers made to current or former political appointees. If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES or Presidential Appointee employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the Human Resources Office. Please ensure you meet the qualification requirements described below. Key Requirements: You must be a U.S. citizen to apply for this position. You must successfully pass a background investigation. Selective Service registration required. Current federal employees must meet time-in-grade requirements. You must be able to obtain and maintain a Government credit card. You must be able to deploy with little or no advance notice to anywhere in the United States and its territories for an extended period of time. Please review the Additional Information section for additional key requirements.
